Have you ever gone to a private school?

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: What's your plan then?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I need to somehow get in with the popular girls.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: I know! Our off-campus field trip to the mall is this weekend. You can impress them then.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: How would I do that?

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Outshop them! They can't make fun of you if your clothes are from the same store.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Like lions hunting on the African plains... They'll respect you if you catch the same prey.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: You mean, if we wear the same Praja shirts?

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: It's like... Survival of the fashionista, as they say.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I don't think that's what they say.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Close enough.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Sounds like a plan.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Status is the only thing that matters in this school.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: If other people treat me with respect, Paige won't matter.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Being popular is the only thing that's going to make me feel better.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: That's not actually going to stop Paige, but...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I don't want to get bullied anymore.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: And the only way stop that is to get to the top.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: That's the way to do it.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: ...And those cream puffs are profiteroles!

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Even I didn't know some of those French ones. Good job!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Thanks.
Sam takes a big bite of her lunch.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: This is delicious!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Delicious? Wow, clearly you have no sense of taste.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Correct names or not, this food is awful.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: The coq a vin is too bitter, the foie gras is low-grade, and the escargot is full of snails!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Come on, girls. I'm going to have my manservant deliver us some `real` food from that patisserie near my French chateau.
nodes.text_bbcode: Come on, girls. I'm going to have my manservant deliver us some [color=#3b78e2][i]real[/i][/color] food from that patisserie near my French chateau.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Like I said, you don't know what you're talking about.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Of course I do. This is clearly some exotic... Dessert... Thing.
Sam takes a big bite of some suspicious paste...
... And spits it out!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Uchh!! I have no idea what that was, but it tasted like pureed duck liver.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: That was foie gras. It `is` pureed duck liver!
nodes.text_bbcode: That was foie gras. It [color=#3b78e2][i]is[/i][/color] pureed duck liver!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: That just makes it worse!

nodes.speaker: Caroline
nodes.text: Ew, that almost made me lose `my` lunch.
nodes.text_bbcode: Ew, that almost made me lose [color=#3b78e2][i]my[/i][/color] lunch.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Gross. You really have no sense of taste.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: This food is textured. The coq a vin is rich, the foie gras is buttery, and the escargot is earthy!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Come on, girls. I'm going to sit next to people that can actually appreciate subtle nuance.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Enjoy your lunch, Bargain Bin.
Paige walks up to Sam and tips her tray into her lap.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Here, I'll help you clean that up.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Seriously, what is their problem?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: It's not like I've done anything to them.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: They're the richest and most popular girls in school, Sam. That's just how they are.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I'm not going to stand for this. It's not about just fitting in anymore.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I can't become rich...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: So I'm going to become popular.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Why?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: This is a matter of...

nodes.text: Hah, yeah right!

nodes.speaker: Ms. Kennedy
nodes.text: Girls! Stop talking. I'd hate to send you to the office for demerits on the first day.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Kennedy
nodes.text: And I'm sure you'd hate to miss your class time.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Yes, Ms. Kennedy.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Kennedy
nodes.text: Now turn your attention to the front. We have professional actors performing Wilford Schlockspeare's 'Spamlet' today!
At lunch, Penelope and Sam sit down at fancy tables with white tablecloths and wait for their food.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: So I guess Paige has it out for you.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Was it her tipping my bow in archery or hitting me with the boom in sailing class that clued you in?

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Sorry, Sam.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: No, I'm sorry. It's just been a bad morning. Why did Paige and the popular girls have to choose me?

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: I'm not sure, but don't look now. She's coming this way!
Paige and her friends walk up to Sam's table.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Why'd we choose you, Bargain Bin? Easy. Penelope's family may only have a couple million, but she's not here on scholarship. You're the odd one out. Right, Prissy?

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: Ugh, I'm sitting over here. I don't want to be touched by the impoverished.

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: My twin sister Missy touched someone in a lower tax bracket, and she had to wear a scarf around her head for weeks to stop it from spreading.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Not having money isn't a disease.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: What she's trying to say is that you don't belong here.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I don't belong here? I got in, didn't I?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Well, of course. Monarch has to do `some` charity to improve its image.
nodes.text_bbcode: Well, of course. Monarch has to do [color=#3b78e2][i]some[/i][/color] charity to improve its image.

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: Yeah, like that time they made us read books to all those dyslexic children.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Whatever, Prissy. You're just bitter because nobody told you to start on the last page and read backwards.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Just ignore them, Sam. Look, here's lunch!
Sam sees waiters carrying huge platters of strange food over.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: What are you going to get?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I'm not sure. It all smells really good.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I bet you don't even know what we're being served.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Of course I do! We're totally eating...
Sam looks at a dish with a creamy sauce with snails.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I prefer my notebook and pen, thanks.

nodes.speaker: Caroline
nodes.text: Oh, how quaint.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: And smart. I heard that writing something down helps you remember it better later.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Whatever. Leave it to the freebie to do things the cheap way.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Give it a rest, Paige.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Unfortunately, it broke down just last week.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Oh really? That's `convenient.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Oh really? That's [color=#3b78e2][i]convenient.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Caroline
nodes.text: And totally not a problem. Why don't you just have, like, your butler bring over your desktop?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Butler?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: She has no butler, Caroline. And if she doesn't have a second house, I doubt she even has a second computer.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Not everyone has to use a laptop, Paige.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: And not everyone has to wear knock-off Sixes jeans, but that doesn't seem to stop Charity Case over there.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: I went to junior high with Paige. She always chooses one girl to pick on.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Last year, she picked on this girl who bit her nails. Paige teased her so mercilessly, the girl chewed all her nails off!

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: The school manicurists couldn't even fix them, and the girl transferred out two weeks into the school year.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: That's kind of gross. But mostly sad.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: I'm lucky they don't pick on me. But my family has some money, so I slip by.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: You can too. If you prove that you can handle yourself.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I'll try that. Thanks for the advice.
Penelope and Sam make it to their first class and sit down.

nodes.speaker: Ms. Kennedy
nodes.text: Good morning! I'm your English teacher, Ms. Kennedy. Please take out your laptops, so we can begin.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Laptops?
Sam watches everyone pull out high-tech laptops from their bags and begin typing on them.
Sam brings out an old notebook and pen.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Too poor to afford a laptop, Bargain Bin?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Shut up, Paige. I'm not using a laptop because...

nodes.prompt: I'm not using a laptop because...

options.label: My laptop is in the shop.

menu.text: I'm not using a laptop because...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Buildings with gold ceilings? That's just unnecessary.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: And it doesn't matter what the classes are like if we're going to be running into Paige.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: She's enough to make life here pretty awful.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: That's an `awfully` sad way to think about it.
nodes.text_bbcode: That's an [color=#3b78e2][i]awfully[/i][/color] sad way to think about it.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Even with Paige, I'm still looking forward to classes at least.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: You're making it sound tougher than it is.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: If Paige would leave me alone, maybe I could be excited about everything else.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: You really think so? But what about yesterday? Paige was really mean to you.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: The world doesn't revolve around Paige. I'm sure there are much nicer people to be friends with.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: And, come on, equestrian class? What girl doesn't want to ride a pony?

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: I'm happy you said that. I was worried that Paige would be hard to deal with, but you're right.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Now if only she'd just leave me alone, I could enjoy everything else.

nodes.speaker: Mom
nodes.text: Anyway, it looks like you're ready to go. Take care of yourself! I'll visit you in a few weeks.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Bye, Mom...
As Sam's mom drives away, Sam picks up her duffle bag and starts walking up to Monarch Prep's dormitory where a crowd of girls are waiting to move in...

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Hey, I'm Penelope, your roommate. I'm new here too.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Nice to meet you.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Hmm... What's this? Last season's jeans and grungy tennis shoes? Looks like someone's here on scholarship.

nodes.speaker: Caroline
nodes.text: Ha ha! You can always spot the freebies, Paige.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Whoa, what's your problem?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Just calling it like I see it. I wouldn't want any one of `us` associating with the wrong crowd.
nodes.text_bbcode: Just calling it like I see it. I wouldn't want any one of [color=#3b78e2][i]us[/i][/color] associating with the wrong crowd.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Some of us don't need to spend thousands of dollars to look good.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Let me guess, you've been slumming it in public school where your kind of look is totally hipster?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Well, newsflash. Monarch Prep is a private school. Girls here not only know what fashion is, we `define` it.
nodes.text_bbcode: Well, newsflash. Monarch Prep is a private school. Girls here not only know what fashion is, we [color=#3b78e2][i]define[/i][/color] it.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Leave her alone. You know we wear uniforms. Maybe she just wore this to move in. Who wants to mess up their nice clothes?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Please. I wouldn't use this girl's shirt as a dust rag.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Just because I don't spend all my time shopping...

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Whatever. I'm out of here.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Yeah, get out. I hope you trip on your Praja heels!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: So much for fitting in. Day one, and someone's already out to get me!
The next morning, Sam and Penelope walk to class.
They pass by the school's colossal gym, the stables, the archery fields, and a cluster of buildings with Gothic, high-vaulted ceilings.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: ...And over there is the lake where we have sailing class, and here's the school library.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: So what's special about the library? Butlers combing the shelves for you? Signed, first edition copies of every book?

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: No, it's just a normal library. Except for the ceilings made of gold.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Wow, okay. That sounds... Shiny. This school is way beyond fancy.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: I know, isn't it great?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: It's `something.`
nodes.text_bbcode: It's [color=#3b78e2][i]something.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Well, thanks for the tour, Penelope. How do you know so much?

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Research. I've wanted to be part of Monarch Prep's fashion design program since I figured out how to dress myself!

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: And everything here is really glamorous. All the girls wear designer brands and high-end vintage clothes.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: When we're not in uniform, of course.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: It's great that you're so happy to be here.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: I love good fashion, and Monarch is totally the 'Paris' of Centerscore.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: But what about you? Aren't you happy to be here?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: The classes sound amazing, but that Paige girl is so stuck-up! I don't want to be a downer though.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I think...

nodes.prompt: I think...

options.label: School will take some getting used to.

nodes.speaker: Mom
nodes.text: You will?

nodes.speaker: Mom
nodes.text: I'm happy to hear that. It might be hard the first couple weeks, but I just know you'll enjoy it here.

nodes.speaker: Mom
nodes.text: Samantha, that's what you say when you're upset.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Well, I `am` upset. I know you're in a bad place with the job and Dad, but...
nodes.text_bbcode: Well, I [color=#3b78e2][i]am[/i][/color] upset. I know you're in a bad place with the job and Dad, but...

nodes.speaker: Mom
nodes.text: But what? Samantha, I'm not thrilled you won't be home, but since Dad's gone, things are changing, and we both have to get used to that.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Great. Now I just feel bad.
The fire starts spreading...
Penelope unwinds the hose as Sam runs out to the dock with it. Penelope twists the valve.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Hurry!
Sam aims the hose at the torch where the boys are...
And a jet of water bursts from the hose, dousing the flames and drenching everyone at the party.

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: My dress!

nodes.speaker: Preston
nodes.text: My dessert!
As the fire dies down, everyone heads inside to dry off.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Well, that was exciting. Good work with the hose.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Yeah. Thanks for helping.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Bargain Bin, hurry up with that hose!
Penelope unwinds the hose as Sam runs out to the dock with it. Penelope twists the valve...
And Sam trips and tangles herself in the hose!
The fire starts spreading...
... And the students watch as the fire eats at the boat then burns itself out.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: My dad's boat... It's gone.
The sailboat sits in the lake, charred and broken.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: I can't believe the boat burned down in the middle of a lake.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Yeah, it seems ironic.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: The hose was a good idea, Sam. Too bad you got tangled in it.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I tried. Thanks for helping anyway.
Colt leaves, slamming the door behind him.

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: He might be cute, but status-wise, he's even beneath `you`, Charity Case.
nodes.text_bbcode: He might be cute, but status-wise, he's even beneath [color=#3b78e2][i]you[/i][/color], Charity Case.

nodes.speaker: Preston
nodes.text: Hey everyone, get outside!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: What's outside?

nodes.speaker: Chad
nodes.text: Dessert! We're lighting the torches for the creme brulees and baked Alaska!
Paige and Sam go outside with the other students.
On the dock, the Spartan boys start striking matches for a very long torch... Right next to an enormous, wooden sailboat.

nodes.speaker: Penelope
nodes.text: Aren't dessert torches supposed to be... Smaller?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Yeah, one wrong move, and the dessert's not the only thing that'll be on fire.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Hey boys, watch it. Get the fire away from that boat!

nodes.speaker: Preston
nodes.text: Gah! Angry Paige!
Surprised, Preston falls, and the torch flies out of his hand onto the deck of the sailboat!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: We have to put that fire out! Prissy? Caroline? Help!

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: I'm not going anywhere near that fiery boat in my Ducky dress. The smoke smell will take forever to come off.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Paige and I aren't exactly friends, but she seems really upset about this. And this'll help me get on Paige's good side.
Sam looks around and sees a garden hose.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Penelope, over there. The hose!

nodes.prompt: Hose down the boat and put out the fire!

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: Good.

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: What? I thought we were cool, Sam, but I guess you're just trying to suck up to this jerk.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Lay off, Prissy. If Sam doesn't want to know him, I certainly do.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I think it's cool having a bad boy at the party.

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: You lay off, Paige. This 'bad boy' ruined our last party by making out with two girls in the same night without telling either of them!

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: I didn't hear any complaints...

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: No. Not until they found out and tore my room apart looking for you!

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: He's a `townie.` As in, he's from the wrong side of town. And he's returning there `now.`
nodes.text_bbcode: He's a [color=#3b78e2][i]townie.[/i][/color] As in, he's from the wrong side of town. And he's returning there [color=#3b78e2][i]now.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: Great. I was just leaving. See you around, `Paige.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Great. I was just leaving. See you around, [color=#e23b3b][i]Paige.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Colt must be really mad at me now.

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: Well, you should `un-meet`!
nodes.text_bbcode: Well, you should [color=#3b78e2][i]un-meet[/i][/color]!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I don't remember putting you in charge of my social life.

nodes.speaker: Prissy
nodes.text: Someone ought to keep you from making bad choices.

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: Whoa, ladies, come on. I'm used to girls fighting over me, but not like this.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Lay off, Prissy. I told you already. You don't decide who is or isn't invited.

nodes.text: Prissy storms off.

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: Wow, what a piece of work. These rich girls think way too much of themselves.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Tell me about it. Who are you?

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: I'm Colt. You?
Before Sam can answer, two boys run up to Sam and Colt.

nodes.speaker: Preston
nodes.text: Hey, buddy, do you know where the kitchen is? We want to serve the creme brulees now.

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: Do I look like I care about your cream whatevers?

nodes.speaker: Preston
nodes.text: N-no. We're just looking for matches to light the creme brulee torch.

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: That's more like it. I have no idea what a 'creme brulee' is, but a `fire` I can help you with.
nodes.text_bbcode: That's more like it. I have no idea what a 'creme brulee' is, but a [color=#e23b3b][i]fire[/i][/color] I can help you with.

nodes.text: Colt tosses the two boys the matchbook in his pocket.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Are you sure you want to do that? They sound like they're up to no good.

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: Please, the biggest problem these kids have faced is figuring out whether to use the gold or silver plates at dinner.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: That is so true.

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: So you from around here?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Ha ha, no. I'm just a regular girl. Not a trust fund baby with a million houses to show for it.

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: 'Regular' is fine by me. That automatically makes you hotter than anyone here.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Thanks. You're actually kind of cool. I wasn't expecting that from a Spartan boy.

nodes.speaker: Colt
nodes.text: Spartan? I'm `way` better than any of those wimpy, prep boys.
nodes.text_bbcode: Spartan? I'm [color=#e23b3b][i]way[/i][/color] better than any of those wimpy, prep boys.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Hey, Bargain Bin!

nodes.speaker: Paige

nodes.text: I can't believe I freaked out about the boat. But it's the only reminder I have of being happy with him.

nodes.text: That makes total sense. I freaked out when my mom started packing my dad's stuff away. Even though my dad left us, I still wanted something to remember him by.

nodes.speaker: Sam

nodes.text: Sounds like we're both pretty pathetic, huh?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: It just sounds like we both miss our dads.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Thanks for that. I feel better.

nodes.text: No, the boat. My dad was so dumb, he named his boat the Key Lime Pie. Who does that?

nodes.text: My dad named his Fjord Anaconda the 'Roquefjord' after the French cheese because it sounded classier.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Ha ha. That's pretty terrible.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I know, right?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: You know what? You're not rich, and you're not fashionable, but you're not bad. You can hang out with me anytime, Bargain Bin.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: The name's Sam.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Fine. You can hang out with me anytime, `Sam.`

nodes.text: Back in present day...

nodes.text: So that's how you and Paige became friends?

nodes.text: I thought you and the Monarch girls were always good friends.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: No way! Well, Penelope was always a friend, but Paige didn't like me until the Key Lime Pie incident.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I never liked the other girls. They just put up with me.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: But wait, Sam, that's the end of the story?!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: No, of course not. It's just the first part.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: How about Colt? How does he fit in? When did you two start dating?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Calm down, calm down.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Backstory. It's important.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: We're coming up to the good part.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I still have to tell you about what happened later that night... After the party...
Wow, looks like there's a lot more to this story!
But for now, feel good about your game! You helped Sam climb to the top of the social ladder!

nodes.speaker: Sam

nodes.text: Enough talk. More tossing!
The Monarch girls and remaining Spartan boys lift Sam...

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Ahhhhh!
And throw her in the lake!
Later...

nodes.speaker: Mom
nodes.text: Okay, Samantha, you ready?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: N-no. I don't want to go.

nodes.speaker: Mom
nodes.text: I know things at Monarch were bad, but you can't hide forever. Going to Centerscore High will be good for you.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: That's what you said right before Monarch. And that was a disaster. I don't believe you!

nodes.speaker: Mom
nodes.text: You can meet new people here, Sam.

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: It doesn't matter. No one's going to like me. They're all going to make fun of me! And throw things at me. And burn my books.

nodes.speaker: Mom
nodes.text: That was Monarch. This is different.

nodes.speaker: Mom
nodes.text: You can make new friends. Or try new things. You always wanted join the cheerleading team, remember?

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: I... I can't do that! That's too much! The cheerleaders are all popular girls!

nodes.speaker: Sam
nodes.text: Just let me stay home! I never want to leave the house again!
Sam is a coward for the rest of her life?! This can't be the right ending!
Do you really want to let it end this way?
Try again and see if you can get a better ending for Sam!
